official_sources.title: GDAL raster mosaic resolution, alignment and overlap policy
official_sources.finding: GDAL raster mosaic checks common raster characteristics, defaults to requiring the same resolution, can align output bounds to the declared resolution, and uses input-list order for overlap priority unless an explicit pixel function is selected.
official_sources.limitation: Target-aligned bounds do not by themselves prove that every source origin lies on the same grid, and a pixel function can change elevation semantics.

official_sources.title: gdalbuildvrt source order, masks, nodata and projection caveat
official_sources.finding: gdalbuildvrt exposes same/highest/lowest/average/common resolution policies, uses the last overlapping input when no pixel function is supplied, uses source masks by default, and warns that allowing projection differences does not reproject the sources.
official_sources.limitation: A valid VRT XML is only a recipe; source immutability, ordering, coverage and exact decoded values still require readback checks.

official_sources.title: GDAL VRT source rectangles, nodata and overview behavior
official_sources.finding: VRT bands map source pixel rectangles to destination rectangles, may contain multiple ordered sources, can expose masks and nodata, and may use source or virtual overviews for downsampled RasterIO requests.
official_sources.limitation: Incorrect source rectangles, hidden nodata or implicit overviews can create plausible but noncanonical extrema.

official_sources.title: gdalwarp alignment, overview and deterministic transformation controls
official_sources.finding: gdalwarp states that target-aligned pixels align output extent to target resolution but not necessarily to the input grid, can automatically use source overviews, and documents that exact transformation with error threshold zero is needed to avoid some tiling-dependent differences.
official_sources.limitation: Warping and resampling alter the native support set, so a mosaic for extrema should remain native-grid unless a reviewed reprojection is unavoidable.

official_sources.title: Rasterio merge compatibility and reverse-painter order
official_sources.finding: Rasterio merge requires compatible band count, data type and CRS, rejects rotated or flipped rasters, and merges valid pixels in listed order using reverse painting by default or explicit first, last, min, max, sum or count methods.
official_sources.limitation: Min or max merge methods compute across overlapping sources and must not be confused with parcel extrema over one canonical terrain surface.

official_sources.title: rio merge output resolution and target alignment controls
official_sources.finding: rio merge exposes explicit output resolution, target-aligned pixels, first/last/min/max/sum/count merge methods, nearest resampling by default, and a highest-resolution versus first-source-resolution choice.
official_sources.limitation: CLI defaults can change output grid or source priority when input order changes; every option and ordered input manifest must be persisted.

official_sources.title: gdal_translate strict native-window extraction and outside-window errors
official_sources.finding: gdal_translate can enforce strict information preservation, select exact full-resolution pixel windows, force base resolution with overview NONE, and fail when a requested window lies partly outside using the error-on-partially-outside option.
official_sources.limitation: Without strict and outside-window error controls, conversion or padding can silently introduce altered values or zeros.

official_sources.title: GDAL tile index footprint, CRS and raster characteristics inventory
official_sources.finding: gdaltindex creates one footprint record per raster, can store source CRS and metadata, filter by pixel size, and recommends explicit target resolution, data type, nodata and mask metadata for GTI use.
official_sources.limitation: Tile-index footprints are bounding rectangles and do not prove valid-data coverage, seam equality or immutable source bytes.
